oil.when: 2018–2019 with the 4.2-inch or 7-inch multi-information display between the gauges
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have been changed, or the scheduled maintenance has been done.

Use the arrow buttons on the left of the steering wheel to reach the settings. On the 4.2-inch display open the Vehicle Settings menu; on the 7-inch display go to the gear-shaped settings icon and press and hold OK to open it.
Choose Scheduled Maintenance and press OK.
Choose Yes. The display shows a message when the reset is complete and the maintenance message goes away.
oil.note: Toyota's maintenance message counts distance; it does not test the oil.

tpms.when: 2018–2019, set from the multi-information display (no reset button)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker. The spare has no sensor.
Do this with cold tires: park somewhere safe and leave the car off for at least 20 minutes first. It cannot be done while moving.
With the steering wheel arrows, open Vehicle Settings (4.2-inch display) or the gear-shaped settings icon (7-inch display, press and hold OK to enter).
Choose TPWS, then Set Pressure, and press and hold OK until the tire pressure light blinks 3 times.
Drive at about 25 mph or faster for roughly 10 to 30 minutes so the system learns the new pressures.
If it has not finished after about an hour of driving, park for about 20 minutes and then drive again.
tpms.note: If the tire pressure light blinks for about a minute and then stays on, the system has a fault. A reset will not clear it; have it checked.
